question: Why is Redis single-threaded, and how does it achieve >100,000 operations per second?
category: Why is Redis single-threaded, and how does it achieve >100,000 operations per second?

options.text: It operates entirely in RAM and uses non-blocking I/O multiplexing (epoll/kqueue), eliminating thread context switches and lock contention.
RDB creates point-in-time binary disk snapshots; AOF logs every write command sequentially for near-zero RPO.
Keys are timestamps; ZREMRANGEBYSCORE removes timestamps older than window; ZCARD checks count; ZADD appends current timestamp.
volatile-lru evicts least recently used keys among those with an expire TTL; allkeys-lru evicts LRU keys across the entire database.

explanation: It operates entirely in RAM and uses non-blocking I/O multiplexing (epoll/kqueue), eliminating thread context switches and lock contention.
